[{"text":"yo","commandType":4},{"text":"conntinue","commandType":4},{"text":"System Scanning and Analysis


The System Scanner module runs with native speed (C++/Rust) and enumerates all hardware and resources. It uses Windows APIs and WMI to query components: e.g. Win32_Processor for CPU name, core count and clock (via a WQL query such as SELECT Name,MaxClockSpeed FROM Win32_Processor
devblogs.microsoft.com
codeproject.com
), Win32_PhysicalMemory for total RAM, and Win32_Volume or GetDiskFreeSpaceEx for storage volumes. NVIDIA’s NVAPI and AMD’s ADL libraries can be employed for GPU details and driver versions
developer.nvidia.com
gpuopen.com
. For example, NVAPI provides “GPU Management: Enumeration of physical and logical GPUs, thermal and cooling controls”
developer.nvidia.com
, and ADL similarly accesses Radeon card info
gpuopen.com
. The scanner also inspects running processes using the ToolHelp API:
cpp
Copy
Edit
HANDLE hSnap = CreateToolhelp32Snapshot(TH32CS_SNAPPROCESS, 0);
PROCESSENTRY32 pe = { sizeof(pe) };
if(Process32First(hSnap, &pe)) {
    do {
        // pe.szExeFile contains process name, pe.th32ProcessID the PID
    } while(Process32Next(hSnap, &pe));
}
CloseHandle(hSnap);
This captures a snapshot of all processes
learn.microsoft.com
. The tool can flag high-CPU tasks or common background services. System health metrics (CPU/GPU load, temperatures, RAM usage) are monitored via sensor libraries (e.g. integrate Open Hardware Monitor or Intel/AMD sensor APIs). Open Hardware Monitor “monitors temperature sensors, fan speeds, voltages, load and clock speeds” for Intel/AMD CPUs and NVIDIA/ATI GPUs
openhardwaremonitor.org
. The collected data feeds the dashboard (current usage, min/max, alerts for throttling or overheating) and identifies bottlenecks (e.g. full RAM, slow disk).
Game Optimization Profiles


We include a Game Optimizer that maintains a database of popular titles (e.g. Valorant, Apex Legends, Minecraft) and recommended settings tailored to the user’s hardware. For each game, the tool can auto-apply optimized configurations (resolution, graphics level, in-game setting files) on launch. It may also enable Windows Game Mode (if applicable) or adjust process priority for the game. GPU vendor APIs help tune graphics: for example, NVIDIA’s NVAPI can tweak GPU clocks or power targets, and AMD’s ADL can adjust Radeon settings, to maximize frame rates. The app can suggest game-specific tweaks (e.g. enabling “Competitive Mode” in Valorant or lowering texture quality) by reading the user’s GPU/CPU tier and using community benchmark data. In essence, this mimics the functionality of GeForce Experience or Radeon Software by auto-optimizing in-game settings based on hardware capability
developer.nvidia.com
gpuopen.com
.
Overclocking Support
For Overclocking, we provide safe auto-adjustment suggestions and live monitoring. GPU overclocking leverages NVAPI or ADL: these SDKs expose clock speed, voltage, and thermal controls for graphics cards
developer.nvidia.com
gpuopen.com
. CPU tuning can integrate with Intel’s XTU or AMD’s Ryzen Master utilities (or use low-level APIs if exposed) to read and write CPU multipliers or voltage. The tool continuously monitors sensor data (core temps, package power) and suggests a small increment (e.g. +5–10%) only if thermals allow. Real-time charts of temperature and clock (via Open Hardware Monitor or Intel Power Gadget) help users see “before/after” effects. For example, Open Hardware Monitor “reads the core temperature sensors of Intel and AMD processors” and GPU sensor data
openhardwaremonitor.org
, so we can warn if an OC attempt causes thermal throttling. The UI can offer predefined profiles (e.g. “Gaming Overclock”, “Silent Mode”) and revert buttons to undo changes on crash.
Driver Management
The Driver Manager scans all installed device drivers and flags outdated ones. It queries the WMI class Win32_PnPSignedDriver, which exposes properties like DriverVersion and DriverDate
learn.microsoft.com
. By iterating through this class, the app lists each device’s current driver version. It then uses the Windows Update Agent (WUA) API to search for newer driver updates: for example, creating an IUpdateSearcher COM object and calling Search for driver updates
learn.microsoft.com
. (WUA’s Search method can filter by device drivers in Windows Catalog.) If a newer WHQL-signed driver is found, the app can download and install it (or link to the vendor page). This ensures trusted updates: NVidia and AMD drivers can also be queried directly via their SDKs or by parsing official web catalogs.
Benchmarking Tools
A Benchmark Engine runs standardized performance tests on demand. For CPU, this might launch a multithreaded workload (e.g. computing large matrix multiplies or running phoronix CPU tests), and for GPU a graphics or compute shader loop. Benchmark results (scores or FPS values) are stored locally (e.g. in SQLite) and compared against baseline metrics for similar hardware. Optionally, results can be uploaded to an online service like OpenBenchmarking.org, which “provides storage of benchmark result data… and tools for sharing results and efficiently comparing multiple test results”
openbenchmarking.org
. The app’s dashboard plots benchmarks over time, so users can spot regressions (e.g. after a driver update). It can also display percentile charts (“your GPU’s score is in the 75th percentile of surveyed cards”) by pulling data from an online API.
Custom OS Optimization
The OS Tuner module applies system-wide tweaks. It can disable unnecessary Windows services and startup programs to free resources. For example, it can stop services like print spooler or telemetry if not needed, and disable them via sc config or WMI’s service interface. These changes are guided by known recommendations: disabling Windows services is known to “quickly improve the performance of the operating system”
itpro.com
. Similarly, it trims startup apps by editing the HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run registry keys or Task Scheduler entries. The Tuner can also apply one-click presets (e.g. “Max Performance” vs. “Balanced”) that adjust system settings: turning off visual effects, setting power scheme to high performance, enabling Game Mode, and cleaning temporary files. All changes include undo options and user confirmations.
User Interface
The application’s UI is built with Electron + React, providing a cross-platform (Win8/10/11) GUI
electronjs.org
. The main process (Node.js) performs privileged tasks (scans, WMI queries, driver updates, benchmark runs) and communicates via IPC to the React front-end, which renders the dashboard and forms. Electron’s multi-process model (Chrome-style) keeps the UI responsive
electronjs.org
: the “main” process (Node) handles system calls, while each BrowserWindow runs React in a sandboxed renderer. The dashboard shows current status, alerts (e.g. “CPU temp high”), and quick actions (one-click optimize, update drivers). A simple mode displays high-level summaries and suggested fixes, while an advanced mode reveals detailed controls (service list, sensor graphs). Modular React components (e.g. <SystemWidget>, <GameProfileList>, <BenchmarkChart>) make the UI extensible. Electron’s ability to create native dialogs and menus is used for confirmations and scheduling tasks (e.g. scheduling overnight scans).
Tech Stack and Components
Backend (C++ or Rust): Implements core scanning, overclocking, and driver logic. Both C++ and Rust offer low-level Windows API access and high performance
bairesdev.com
. Rust’s memory safety is a plus, while C++ has mature Win32 bindings.
Frontend (Electron/React): Cross-platform UI using web tech. Electron “embeds Chromium and Node.js to enable desktop applications”
electronjs.org
. React manages the componentized interface.
Data Persistence: SQLite is used for local storage (system snapshots, benchmark history, config). SQLite is “often used as the on-disk file format for desktop applications” like record-keeping and media suites
sqlite.org
, making it a natural choice for caching scan results. (Alternatively, a lightweight NoSQL like LevelDB or NeDB could be used for JSON-like storage.)
Key modules include: SystemScanner (hardware/WMI queries), GameOptimizer (per-game settings), OverclockManager, DriverManager, BenchmarkEngine, OSTuner, and a central Settings/Logger. Communication between frontend and backend happens via Electron’s IPC or a local web socket, with REST or JSON-RPC style messages.
Example UI Flow
Dashboard View: On launch, the app immediately scans and displays overall health (CPU/GPU utilization, temps, RAM/disk usage). Critical alerts (e.g. “High CPU temp”) are highlighted. A summary widget suggests “Optimize System” or “Update Drivers” actions.
One-Click Optimize: Clicking “Optimize” runs a quick sweep: stops idle services, cleans temp files, applies registry tweaks. A progress bar shows steps. On completion, the UI shows achieved gains (e.g. +10% free RAM).
Driver Updates: The Driver tab lists devices and driver versions. The user clicks “Check for Updates”, which runs WUA in the background and populates a list of available driver updates. The user can review and install each.
Game Profiles: In the Games tab, installed games are detected (via Steam/Epic folders or manual add). Selecting a game shows recommended settings and a “Apply” button, which writes config changes. An “Advanced” switch opens flags for GPU overclock or Windows priority tweaks.
Benchmark: In the Benchmarks tab, the user runs CPU or GPU tests. Results appear on a line chart vs. past runs and versus online baselines. Tooltips indicate percentiles.
Settings: Options allow enabling auto-optimization on schedule, selecting performance vs. quiet profiles, and toggling advanced features.
Through this architecture, the PC Optimizer provides a unified, extensible framework for scanning, analysis, and tuning across all user types – from gamers (performance mode) to professionals (stability mode). Each component uses well-known Windows mechanisms and vendor SDKs as described, ensuring both safety and effectiveness. Sources: System scanning uses WMI (Win32_Processor, Win32_PnPSignedDriver)

; performance gains from disabling services are documented

; embedded DB via SQLite
